title: Remapping shortcuts to include a remapped key works inconsistently

judgment.rationale: The long-running thread collects several distinct Keyboard Manager symptoms and configurations, including recent lost-shortcut and W-key-repeat reports. They do not establish a single defect; the old generic log request is not a useful next action.
evidence: The original report concerns shortcuts that include a remapped key and says behavior is inconsistent.
Later comments describe different remap combinations, shortcut loss, and a W-key repeating until PowerToys is closed; the reports do not provide one common minimal repro.
Quick Accent false-start key-up handling was changed in PR #49644, but that known fix does not establish the cause of the other Keyboard Manager reports in this thread.
judgment.recommended_action: Split the distinct recent symptoms into exact, independently reproducible sequences before assigning one code owner or fix.

fix_assessment.rationale: The thread combines multiple key mappings and failure modes without a shared minimal reproduction; a single fix hypothesis would overstate the available evidence.

issue_context.summary: A broad Keyboard Manager issue contains inconsistent shortcut remapping reports and later reports of distinct global key symptoms.
known_information: The body describes shortcuts that include a remapped key and labels the area Keyboard Manager.
Comments describe varied mappings and symptoms, including shortcuts ceasing to work and a W key repeating until PowerToys exits.
Some historical discussion requested diagnostic logs, but no single current reproduction is distilled from those requests.
inferences: These reports may represent more than one defect or configuration; the thread title does not establish a common root cause.
The Quick Accent key-up fix in #49644 may overlap a false-start symptom but is not evidence that it resolves the Keyboard Manager reports.
issue_context.analysis: Do not repeat a generic log request or retrofit one hypothesis to a heterogeneous thread. A maintainer should first partition reports by exact remap, triggering application, and whether failure persists after disabling the mapping or module.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and all 31 comments; current labels are Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-Keyboard Manager.
Reviewed #49644 as nearby history; its Quick Accent event pass-through change is specific and does not establish a fix for this issue.

information_gaps.information: Which distinct reported symptom still reproduces on a current build, with its exact source/destination mapping and numbered key sequence.
information_gaps.why_needed: The thread combines shortcut loss, remap inconsistency, and repeated-key reports that cannot be assigned to one owner without identifying a current minimal case.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with one symptom at a time, current PowerToys version, source and destination keys, focused application, numbered actions, expected versus actual result, and whether disabling only that remap restores behavior.

comment.body: This thread now includes different symptoms, including shortcut remaps that stop working and a W key that repeats until PowerToys is closed. To avoid treating them as one defect, could you identify which one still reproduces on a current PowerToys build and provide only that case's source/destination mapping, focused app, numbered key sequence, expected versus actual result, and whether disabling that single remap restores behavior?
